svg.aria-label: Keystone user flow mapped onto the AI-native SDLC playbook
svg.text: How Keystone runs the AI-native SDLC playbook
Top: the playbook's stages (Anthropic). Below: what you type in Claude Code. Every stage ends with a committed file.

g.text: 🔒 draft: no code edits until Approve
🔒 push of this plan's commits closed until verify
🔒 FAIL → /keystone:fix verify, all findings in one pass · UNPROVEN → prove or accept

svg.text: regression test as a new file)
Design is folded into the plan — no separate spec.md; every plan row cites an intent line (I-n). Grill runs inside intent; check runs inside plan.
/keystone-status any time: plan, tasks, gates and cost by stage — answered without a model call. Lift a gate: Status: abandoned or KEYSTONE_GATES=off.
Models by role — Opus judges (intent, plan, check, the verifier) · Sonnet runs implement and verify · scripts do the mechanics (base, files, tests).
Above the prompt — plan and context bars, Next buttons, file links; a handoff to a clean session when the context grows.
Run implement and verify in a fresh session (/clear): every turn re-reads the whole context, so a stage at 500k tokens costs several times more.
